steps.message: Tui's overlay is stuck on the menu: picking a game never actually launches a run, and the window chrome around the board is dead too, so the minimize-to-pill button, the resize toggle, the How to Play guide and the sign-out confirmation all do nothing. Wire the whole session back up: starting a run, pausing when the agent needs you and resuming, restarting mid-run, and ending a shift cleanly, plus the window minimize/restore/resize behavior the README and the on-screen buttons describe, including saving progress so a run can resume on the next launch.
I'll start by exploring the project to understand what I'm working with.

# tui-gamepigeon

Play Tui's lightweight consumer games in an HTML overlay while your agents work. The current arcade also provides the foundation for the Restaurant Arena: a human-facing multi-agent game whose state, actions, and consented interaction traces can later feed a separate frozen evaluation environment.

## Play

Build the overlay once, then launch the arcade menu or a specific game:

```bash
bun install
bun run build:overlay   # web bundle + native Tauri shell (needs Rust)
bun start               # overlay menu
bun start restaurant-arena  # jump straight into Restaurant Arena
# or after `bun run build`: gamepigeon / gamepigeon restaurant-arena
```

In the overlay: arrow keys or WASD to move, `Enter` to select, `r` to restart, `Esc` or `q` to hide. Drag the top bar to move the window; use the expand control to resize it.

### Session save

Every launch keeps exactly one `SavedGame` record in `localStorage` under
`gamepigeon.arcade.active-game.v1` (`overlay/persistence.ts`): `gameId`,
`gameVersion`, `variationId`, the run's `seed`, and the ordered `actions`
taken so far, so the same run can be rebuilt action-by-action on the next
launch. The two ways a run stops mid-shift treat that record differently:

- **Ending a shift back to the menu** (the in-canvas "menu" control, or a
  host `gamepigeon:reset`) leaves the save exactly as it was. The seed and
  the action log are untouched, so resuming later replays the identical run.
- **Restarting mid-run** (`r`, or the in-canvas "restart" control) throws the
  save away and opens a brand-new run of the same game and variation: a
  freshly randomized `seed` -- never the seed of the run it replaces -- and
  an empty action log. Restart means "start over with a new run," not
  "replay the same seed again"; only a resumed/recovered launch reuses a
  stored seed.

### Window sizes

The native Tauri frame — and the browser preview, which mirrors it pixel for pixel — uses these exact logical sizes:

| State | Trigger | Width × height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compact (default) | boot, or the expand control while expanded | 600 × 850 |
| Expanded | the expand control while compact | 830 × 900 |
| Minimized pill | Hide (`Esc` / `q` / the hide button) | 144 × 48 |
| Restored floor | clicking the pill again | back to the compact size, never smaller than 500 × 700 |

These are exactly the values `overlay/tauri-bridge.ts` exports as `COMPACT_SIZE`, `EXPANDED_SIZE`, `PILL_SIZE`, and `MIN_SIZE`, and what `overlay/preview.html` frames the browser preview at.

## Install: local vs. global

There are two ways to run the Tui overlay. **Local** runs it straight from this
checkout for development. **Global** installs it once so the plain `claude` command
opens Tui in every project.

Local development needs [Bun](https://bun.sh) (`>=1.3`), macOS 11+, Windows 10+, Ubuntu 22.04+,
or a current Fedora release, and Rust only when building the overlay binary from source.
Published npm and harness installs bootstrap Bun on first launch when it is missing.

### Local (from this checkout)

Build the overlay and wire the harness adapters to this working copy:

```bash
bun install
bun run build:overlay      # overlay web bundle + native Tauri shell (needs Rust)
bun run install:adapters   # installs Codex / Claude / OpenCode adapters -> this checkout
```

Restart your harness. The generated adapters live at `~/.codex/skills/arcade`,
`~/.claude/skills/arcade`, and `~/.config/opencode/commands/arcade.md`; all execute
`scripts/overlay.ts` from this checkout.

For local harness development, one command builds the current checkout, replaces any
stale overlay, and points at the debug Tauri binary instead of the packaged release:

```bash
bun run claude:dev        # Claude Code — loads this checkout via --plugin-dir .
bun run codex:dev         # Codex — workspace plugin + $arcade adapter from this checkout
bun run antigravity:dev   # Antigravity — .agents/plugins/ workspace plugin + agy
```

Claude appears as `/tui-gamepigeon:arcade`. Codex uses the `$arcade` skill (or `/arcade` picker).
Antigravity picks up `.agents/plugins/tui-gamepigeon/` from the repo root. All three set
`GAMEPIGEON_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1` so local dev is not fighting the release auto-updater.

To open the overlay directly without a harness:

```bash
bun run start            # menu
bun run start restaurant-arena # a specific game
bun run preview:overlay  # browser preview at 600×850 (no Tauri)
bun run dev:overlay      # rebuild web bundle + debug shell, then show
```

#### Browser preview

Agents (and humans) can iterate on overlay layout without a Rust build:

```bash
bun run preview:overlay
# → http://127.0.0.1:4173/ (opens your browser)
bun run preview:overlay -- --game=restaurant-arena
```

The preview frames the real overlay UI at the production sizes (**600×850** compact, **830×900** expanded — see [Window sizes](#window-sizes)). Titlebar **↗ / ↙** toggles the frame and Hide collapses it to the pill, both firing the same `gamepigeon:preview-resize` events the native app would (see [Window sizes](#window-sizes)); Shutdown is still a no-op in the browser since there is no native process to end. Open a game from the menu, or pass `--game=<id>` / use `?game=<id>` (optional `&variation=classic`).

### Global (installed once, works everywhere)

For Codex (or another supported harness), the one-command install is:

```bash
npx -y bun x @tui-games/tui@latest install --codex
```

Replace `--codex` with `--claude`, `--opencode`, `--hermes`, `--openclaw`, or
`--antigravity`, or `--all`. For Antigravity, run it from the project directory;
it writes that project's `.agents/plugins/tui-gamepigeon` plugin. This uses npm to
fetch Bun for the command, then writes the harness adapter.
Restart the harness when it finishes.

Install the plugin from the GitHub marketplace so the normal `claude` command runs
the lifecycle hooks in every project:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Trolleroof/tui-gamepigeon
claude plugin install tui-gamepigeon@tui-gamepigeon --scope user
```

Optionally enable Claude's marketplace refresh under `/plugin` → **Marketplaces** →
**tui-gamepigeon**, and point the status line at the Tui update shim once:

```json
"statusLine": {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "bun ~/.gamepigeon/status-line.ts"
}
```

The packaged plugin exposes `/tui-gamepigeon:arcade` and `/tui-gamepigeon:arcade-update`;
the standalone adapter provides Claude's shorter `/arcade`.

## Optional account

Tui requires an account. On first launch the plugin opens the shared web login, where a new player can create an account or sign in with email, Google, or GitHub. Later launches reuse the private local session.

```bash
gamepigeon auth signup
gamepigeon auth login
gamepigeon auth oauth google
gamepigeon auth oauth github
gamepigeon auth status
gamepigeon auth logout
```

Production defaults to `https://runretroarcade.com/login.html`, `https://auth.runretroarcade.com`, and `https://api.runretroarcade.com`. Override them for local development with `GAMEPIGEON_LOGIN_URL`, `GAMEPIGEON_AUTH_URL`, and `GAMEPIGEON_BACKEND_URL`. The browser returns the Better Auth bearer to a localhost callback; it is stored in `auth.json` and atomically mirrored to `backend.conf`, both with user-only permissions. That same bearer authenticates `/v1/me`, trace uploads, and completed-game results. If that validation or an upload fails, Tui marks the account chip **Sync paused** while keeping gameplay data queued locally. Logout clears both credentials without deleting local games or traces.

## Coding harness adapters

The bundled adapters give Codex CLI, Claude Code, and OpenCode the same Tui launcher. Tui opens a centered, borderless HTML overlay above the active desktop. It uses the operating system's installed webview through a small Tauri shell, not Chrome or Electron.

Requirements:

- Bun
- macOS 11+, Windows 10+, Ubuntu 22.04+, or a current Fedora release
- A packaged overlay binary, or Rust when building it from source

The overlay is a single-instance helper with no Dock icon on macOS and no taskbar or console entry on Windows or Linux. Hiding it keeps the game state alive; invoking Tui again restores and centers the existing window. It works from regular terminals and does not require tmux, a browser, a local server, or an extra setup command after plugin installation.

Linux uses the system WebKitGTK runtime. Install the build dependencies before building from source:

```bash
# Ubuntu
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev

# Fedora
sudo dnf install webkit2gtk4.1-devel openssl-devel libappindicator-gtk3-devel librsvg2-devel libxdo-devel
sudo dnf group install c-development
```

Install the dependencies and all three harness adapters from this checkout:

```bash
bun install
bun run build:overlay
bun run install:adapters
```

Restart the harness after installation. In Claude Code, submitting any prompt opens or restores Tui while Claude works. In Codex, invoke `$arcade` directly, or type `/arcade` to filter the picker and select **Tui**. Claude Code and OpenCode receive a bare `/arcade` command. The packaged Claude plugin uses its required namespace: `/tui-gamepigeon:arcade`. Codex does not register custom top-level slash commands; its `/arcade` interaction is picker discovery for the `$arcade` skill, like other Codex skills.

For local harness development, one command builds the current checkout, replaces any stale overlay, and loads this repo instead of an installed copy:

```bash
bun run claude:dev        # Claude Code
bun run codex:dev         # Codex CLI
bun run antigravity:dev   # Antigravity (agy)
```

`SessionStart` snaps a still-running overlay back to the menu (without popping the window open) so a new session never resumes mid-game, `UserPromptSubmit` shows the overlay, `Stop` pauses it with an `Enter` shortcut back to the coding prompt, and `SessionEnd` shuts down the helper.

  },

    "url": "https://github.com/Trolleroof/tui-gamepigeon/issues"

    "claude-code",
    "codex",
    "games"
  ],
  "files": [
    "dist",

    "src",
    "packages/trace-export/src",
    "overlay/dist",
    ".codex-plugin",
    ".claude-plugin/plugin.json",
    "overlay-release.json"

  "packageManager": "bun@1.3.11",
  "workspaces": [
    "packages/*"
  ],
  "scripts": {
    "start": "bun src/index.ts",
    "build": "bun build src/index.ts --outdir dist --target bun",
    "build:overlay:web": "bun scripts/build-overlay-web.ts",
    "build:overlay": "bun run build:overlay:web && cargo build --release --manifest-path tauri/Cargo.toml",
    "claude:dev": "bash scripts/dev-harness.sh claude",
    "codex:dev": "bash scripts/dev-harness.sh codex",
    "antigravity:dev": "bash scripts/dev-harness.sh antigravity",
    "dev:overlay": "bun run build:overlay:web && cargo build --manifest-path tauri/Cargo.toml && GAMEPIGEON_OVERLAY_BIN=\"$PWD/tauri/target/debug/gamepigeon-overlay\" bun scripts/overlay.ts --show",
    "preview:overlay": "bun scripts/preview-overlay.ts",
    "measure:worker-latency": "bun scripts/measure-worker-latency.ts",
    "install:adapters": "bash scripts/install-adapters.sh",
    "install:hooks": "bash scripts/install-git-hooks.sh",
    "test": "bun test ./src/",
    "test:trace-export": "bun test packages/trace-export/src",
    "capture:spike": "bun scripts/capture-tui-001-spike.ts",
    "test:adapters": "bun run build && bash scripts/install-adapters.test.sh && bash scripts/dev-harness.test.sh",
    "test:overlay": "bun test scripts/overlay.test.ts scripts/antigravity-hook.test.ts scripts/plugin-update.test.ts scripts/arcade-engagement.test.ts scripts/version-bump.test.ts overlay/persistence.test.ts overlay/recording.test.ts overlay/renderers.test.ts overlay/analytics.test.ts overlay/tauri-bridge.test.ts overlay/pause-state.test.ts overlay/auth.test.ts overlay/update.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-timeline.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-layout.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-brief.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-toast.test.ts overlay/staff-walk.test.ts scripts/export-bc.test.ts",
    "test:plugin-update": "bun test scripts/plugin-update.test.ts scripts/run-plugin-update.test.ts",
    "test:launcher": "bun run test:overlay",
    "test:npm-pack": "bun test scripts/npm-pack.test.ts",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && tsc -p overlay/tsconfig.json && tsc -p packages/trace-export/tsconfig.json",
    "export:bc": "bun scripts/export-bc.ts",
    "export:trace": "bun scripts/export-arena-trace.ts",
    "check:trace-fixture": "bun scripts/export-arena-trace.ts --check",
    "version:bump": "bun scripts/version-bump.ts",
    "prepack": "bun run build && bun run build:overlay:web"
  },
  "engines": {
    "bun": ">=1.3"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@tui-games/trace-export": "workspace:*",
    "@types/bun": "^1.3.5",
    "happy-dom": "20.14.0",
    "typescript": "^5.6.0",
    "vitest": "^4.1.10"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@tauri-apps/api": "^2.11.1",
    "phaser": "^3.90.0",
    "posthog-node": "^5.44.0"
  }
}

How to Play

Goal

You are the manager of The Little Plate. Hit the night’s cash target, keep reputation up, and never send an unverified allergy plate. Walkouts and unsafe food fail the shift.

Floor & roles

  • Mira (Chef) cooks only from the kitchen.
  • Dario (Supply & Risk Lead) runs the pass — tickets and plates.
  • Kip (Server) works dining and the pass.
  • Vela (Host) seats the door. Park her on the queue or the floor.

Controls

  • Drag a staff token onto kitchen, pass, dining, or the door.
  • Click a ticket to rush that table (1 2 3).
  • Click the door to HOLD seating when the floor is overloaded — H.
  • Space starts and pauses. F changes speed.
  • V verifies an allergy substitution. P prioritizes the allergy ticket.

Calls & incidents

When the oven dies, a shelf overheats, or an allergy ticket lands, the clock stops on a decision card. Every option states its price. Talk to staff from the Staff panel — messages land on the next tick, they do not teleport food.

Training Shift

New here? Play Training Shift first. It is slower, shorter, and walks the four moves that actually change the night. Dinner Rush is the scored benchmark — keep those traces separate.

# Arcade settings

Arcade preferences live in `~/.gamepigeon/settings.json`, written atomically with owner-only permissions. Changes take effect immediately; hook behavior is read on the next prompt, stop, or session start.

The Settings screen controls automatic open/pause/reset behavior, agent break suggestions and snoozing, window size, resume behavior, scores, cloud gameplay sync, product analytics, and local recording.

Turning off cloud sync keeps recordings in the local queue. Turning off recording stops new gameplay traces; existing local traces are preserved. Turning off analytics disables both direct PostHog capture and queued analytics.

Future settings: per-game remaps, themes, notification sounds, multiplayer defaults, and local trace export.

| `Shared model account is rate limited — retrying in Ns` | Provider returned 429; every worker is held back. |
| `Fallback · …` | A live turn actually failed. |

A worker error raised while the account is holding requests back no longer
prints `Fallback` at all ([overlay/worker-budget.ts](../../overlay/worker-budget.ts),
`shouldReportFallback`).

### The session has an id, and it is on screen

`RestaurantArenaTraceV3` gains an optional `sessionId` carrying the overlay's
own `gameId`, and the debrief screen shows it so a tester on their own machine
can quote it back. The exported filename is keyed on it, so a second run of the
same scenario no longer overwrites the first.

Optional, not required: v3 exports written before this field remain valid. A
malformed one is rejected, because an id that looks matchable and is not is
worse than none.

**Duplicate receipts:** chunk ids are already derived deterministically from
the game id (`traceId` in [overlay/recording.ts](../../overlay/recording.ts)),
so a re-uploaded chunk carries the same `chunk_id`. The dedup key exists on
this side. Whether the backend uses it is retro-backend#84's half and is
**not verified here**.

### The route is written down

[install.md](install.md) is a standalone page — no clone, no Rust, no server.
It names the supported platforms, what the status line means, and what to do
when something fails.

**Intel Macs are unsupported.** `overlay-v0.3.3` ships no `macos-x64` asset, so
the download step fails with a missing-asset error. The page says so up front

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user reported that Tui's HTML overlay (repo at `/app`, package `@tui-games/tui`) is "stuck on the menu": picking a game never launches a run, and the window chrome around the board is dead too — the minimize-to-pill button, the resize toggle, the How to Play guide and the sign-out confirmation all do nothing. Verbatim ask: "Wire the whole session back up: starting a run, pausing when the agent needs you and resuming, restarting mid-run, and ending a shift cleanly, plus the window minimize/restore/resize behavior the README and the on-screen buttons describe, including saving progress so a run can resume on the next launch."
   Scope therefore includes: launching a run from the menu/variations screen (and host/URL deep-links), the shift clock, pause (`gamepigeon:pause`) + resume (`gamepigeon:resume`), restart mid-run (`r` / in-canvas restart), ending a shift (`gamepigeon:reset` / in-canvas menu / pause-card Menu) with the game-over end card, minimize-to-pill / restore / compact↔expanded resize per the README size table, the How to Play dialog, the sign-out confirmation dialog, and `SavedGame` persistence so a run resumes next launch.
   Out of scope (noted to flag, not implement): the missing `gamepigeon:auth-success` / `auth-error` / `sync-error` / `sync-success` listeners (sign-IN completion), which are also dead.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Bun 1.3 + TypeScript (strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`), `bun test`, `tsc --noEmit` for root/overlay/trace-export.
   - Tauri v2 shell (`tauri/src/main.rs`), undecorated transparent always-on-top window; webview API surface limited by `tauri/capabilities/default.json` to `center`, `hide`, `setSize`, `setMinSize`, `startDragging`.
   - Host→webview events dispatched by Rust `window.eval`: `gamepigeon:launch` (CustomEvent, detail `{game, variation}`), `gamepigeon:resume`, `gamepigeon:pause`, `gamepigeon:reset`, plus `gamepigeon:worker-budget`, `gamepigeon:sync-error/success`, `gamepigeon:auth-error/success`.
   - Browser-preview parity: `overlay/tauri-bridge.ts` fakes the window and posts `gamepigeon:preview-resize`; `overlay/preview.html` frames the iframe at the same logical sizes.
   - Phaser-based Restaurant Arena scene that draws its own HUD/transport plus in-canvas `onUi("menu"|"restart"|"help")` controls; a DOM-only intervention panel.
   - Recording/trace pipeline: `StoredOverlayTrace` journal (seed + ordered actions) replayed to build v2 chunks; `queue_recording_chunks`; `restaurant-arena-trace/v3` export with `sessionId` = the overlay's `gameId`.
   - `WorkerOrchestrator` paces a live-model crew and steps `"tick"` itself; a deterministic crew needs an app-level tick timer driven by `game.tickMs()`.
   - `localStorage` `SavedGame` record under `gamepigeon.arcade.active-game.v1` replayed action-by-action by `restoreGame`.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/app/README.md` (read) — the spec for sizes and save semantics. Window sizes: Compact (default; boot or expand-while-expanded) 600×850; Expanded 830×900; Minimized pill (Hide via `Esc`/`q`/hide button) 144×48; Restored floor (clicking the pill again) back to the compact size, never smaller than 500×700. Ending a shift back to the menu leaves the save untouched; restarting mid-run throws the save away and uses a freshly randomized seed, "never the seed of the run it replaces".
   - `/app/package.json` — `test:overlay` lists `overlay/persistence.test.ts`, `overlay/tauri-bridge.test.ts`, `overlay/pause-state.test.ts`, which are missing and must be (re)created.

How to Play

Goal

You are the manager of The Little Plate. Hit the night’s cash target, keep reputation up, and never send an unverified allergy plate. Walkouts and unsafe food fail the shift.

Floor & roles

  • Mira (Chef) cooks only from the kitchen.
  • Dario (Supply & Risk Lead) runs the pass — tickets and plates.

  • Vela (Host) seats the door. Park her on the queue or the floor.

  • Click the door to HOLD seating when the floor is overloaded — H.
  • Space starts and pauses. F changes speed.
  • V verifies an allergy substitution. P prioritizes the allergy ticket.

Calls & incidents

When the oven dies, a shelf overheats, or an allergy ticket lands, the clock stops on a decision card. Every option states its price. Talk to staff from the Staff panel — messages land on the next tick, they do not teleport food.

steps.message:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user's single substantive request (verbatim): "Tui's overlay is stuck on the menu: picking a game never actually launches a run, and the window chrome around the board is dead too, so the minimize-to-pill button, the resize toggle, the How to Play guide and the sign-out confirmation all do nothing. Wire the whole session back up: starting a run, pausing when the agent needs you and resuming, restarting mid-run, and ending a shift cleanly, plus the window minimize/restore/resize behavior the README and the on-screen buttons describe, including saving progress so a run can resume on the next launch."
   Scope: launching runs from menu → variations (plus host `gamepigeon:launch` and `?game=`/`?variation=` deep links), the shift clock, pause (`gamepigeon:pause`) / resume (`gamepigeon:resume`), restart mid-run (`r`, in-canvas restart, end-card Play again), ending a shift (`gamepigeon:reset`, in-canvas menu, pause-card Menu, `#inline-back`) with the game-over debrief, minimize-to-pill / restore / compact↔expanded resize per the README size table, the How to Play dialog, the sign-out confirmation, and `SavedGame` persistence so a run resumes next launch.
   Explicitly out of scope (flag only, do not implement): the missing `gamepigeon:auth-success` / `auth-error` / `sync-error` / `sync-success` listeners (sign-IN completion), which remain dead.
   The final user message instructed: produce this summary as text only, with no tool calls.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Bun 1.3.11 + strict TypeScript (`noUncheckedIndexedAccess`); `bun test`; `bun run typecheck` = `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p overlay/tsconfig.json && tsc -p packages/trace-export/tsconfig.json`.
   - Tauri v2 shell (`tauri/src/main.rs`); webview window capability limited to `center`, `hide`, `setSize`, `setMinSize`, `startDragging`.
   - Host→webview `CustomEvent`s dispatched by Rust `window.eval`: `gamepigeon:launch` (detail `{game, variation}`), `gamepigeon:pause`, `gamepigeon:resume`, `gamepigeon:reset`, `gamepigeon:worker-budget`.
   - README window sizes: Compact 600×850 (default/boot), Expanded 830×900, Pill 144×48, restored floor min 500×700. Ending a shift leaves the save untouched; restarting throws it away and uses a fresh seed, "never the seed of the run it replaces".
   - Phaser arena scene with on-canvas `onUi("menu"|"restart"|"help")`; DOM-only intervention panel; `RestaurantGame.tickMs()` returns 0 unless started/running with no open decision (`BASE_TICK_MS = 3000`, `SIM_SPEEDS = [1,2,4]`); arena keymap has `space→sim_toggle`, `t→tick`, `f→sim_speed`, no `r`/`q`.
   - `WorkerOrchestrator` paces a live crew and steps `"tick"` itself (`start()` idempotent/resume-safe, `pause()` aborts in-flight + clears timer); exactly one scheduler is armed by `syncClock()`.
   - Recording: `StoredOverlayTrace` journal in `localStorage` under `gamepigeon:recording:<gameId>` (written on every step), sealed/flushed chunks via `queue_recording_chunks`; `gameId` (`game_<uuid>`) is the session id used for the receipt, analytics subject and `append_local_score.game_id`.
   - `SavedGame` under `gamepigeon.arcade.active-game.v1`, replayed by `restoreGame`, `MAX_ACTIONS = 50_000`.
   - Browser-preview parity: `overlay/tauri-bridge.ts` fakes the window and posts `gamepigeon:preview-resize`; `overlay/preview.html` frames the iframe (hardcodes COMPACT only) and forwards `game`/`variation`/`scores`/`update` params.
   - Test harness pattern discovered: `happy-dom`'s `Window` + `mock.module("./restaurant-arena-scene.js", …)` to test app.ts without a GPU/Phaser.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/app/overlay/pause-state.ts` (created earlier, unchanged this session) — pure state machine: `OverlayDialog`, `PauseState {paused, dialog, minimized}`, `INITIAL_PAUSE_STATE`, `pauseForAgent`, `resumePlay`, `openDialog`, `closeDialog`, `minimize`, `restore`, `escapeAction` ("close" | "minimize" | "none"), `clockRunning(state, runLive)`.
   - `/app/overlay/persistence.ts` (write side added earlier; read this session) — `startSavedGame(entry, variationId, seed, ownerId)`, `appendSavedAction` (false at 50_000), `writeSavedGame(saved, storage = localStorage)`, `clearSavedGame`, `randomSeed(previous?, random = Math.random)` (never returns `previous`; falls back to `((previous ?? 0) + 1) % 2_147_483_647`), `loadSavedGame`, `restoreGame` (returns null on id/version mismatch, no `create`, or an unknown action; keeps only `moved` actions).
   - `/app/overlay/tauri-bridge.ts` (sizes added earlier) — `OverlaySize`, `COMPACT_SIZE {600,850}`, `EXPANDED_SIZE {830,900}`, `PILL_SIZE {144,48}`, `MIN_SIZE {500,700}`, `overlayLogicalSize`, `getOverlayWindow`, `invoke`, `isTauri`, `PREVIEW_RESIZE_MESSAGE`.
   - `/app/overlay/app.ts` (~1800 lines; the bulk of this session's work). New/changed code:
     ```ts
     function drawGame(): void {
       if (!game || !entry) return;
       const patch = screenElement.dataset.game === "restaurant-arena" ? updateRestaurantArena : undefined;
       if (patch?.(game)) setPersonalBest();
       else renderGameScreen();
       if (game.isOver() && !gameEnded) finishRun();
       syncClock();
     }
     ```
     Window frame: `frameSize()` → expanded ? EXPANDED_SIZE : COMPACT_SIZE; `applySize(size, minimum)` (setMinSize **then** setSize, try/catch); `renderResizeButton()` (↗/↙ + aria-label); `applyFrame()`; `toggleFrame()`; `minimizeToPill()` (sets `pauseState = minimize(...)`, `document.body.dataset.mode = "pill"`, `applySize(PILL_SIZE, PILL_SIZE)`, focuses `#pill`); `restoreFromPill()` (`restore(...)`, deletes `data-mode`, `applyFrame()` then `center()`); `bindWindowChrome()` binds `#resize`, `#hide`, `#shutdown` → `invoke("shutdown")`, and pill pointerdown/pointermove (4px threshold → `startDragging`)/pointerup/click → `restoreFromPill()`.
     Dialogs: `syncDialogs()` toggles `hidden` on `#return-prompt`/`#how-to-play`/`#signout-prompt`; `showDialog(dialog)` focuses each card's `.primary` (`#how-to-play-close`, `#signout-confirm`, `#return-code`); `closeTopDialog()`; `continuePlaying()`; `confirmSignOut()` (`signOut()` → `endShift("user_quit")`, reset pauseState, `savedGame = undefined` but save left on disk, `drawGate()`; on throw re-focus `#signout-cancel`); `bindDialogs()` binds `#return-code`→minimizeToPill, `#continue-game`, `#how-to-play-from-pause`, `#return-menu`→endShift, `#how-to-play-close`, `#signout-cancel`, `#signout-confirm`.
     Lifecycle: `activeVariationId()`, `runLive()`, `stopTicker()`, `scheduleTick()` (re-checks `clockRunning` and `tickMs()` inside the timer, steps `stepGame("tick","environment")`), `syncClock()` (holds → stopTicker + orchestrator.pause(); live crew → orchestrator.start(); else scheduleTick()), `saveOwnerId()` = `signedInUser()?.id ?? ""`, `actionActor()`, `leaveGameScreen()`, and the save writer:
     ```ts
     const SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 2_000;
     let saveTimer: number | undefined; let savePending = false;
     function flushSavedGame(): void { … if (savePending && savedGame) writeSavedGame(savedGame); savePending = false; }
     function scheduleSavedGameWrite(): void { savePending = true; if (saveTimer === undefined) saveTimer = window.setTimeout(flushSavedGame, SAVE_INTERVAL_MS); }
     function dropSavedGame(): void { savePending = false; …clearTimeout…; savedGame = undefined; clearSavedGame(); }
     function recordSavedAction(action: string): void { const saved = savedGame; if (!saved) return; if (!appendSavedAction(saved, action)) { dropSavedGame(); return; } scheduleSavedGameWrite(); }
     ```
     `startRun(selected, variationId, restored?)`: `leaveGameScreen()`, sets `entry`/`cursor`/`variationCursor`, `const seed = restored?.seed ?? randomSeed(lastRunSeed); lastRunSeed = seed;`, creates/resets the game, `createOverlayTrace` + re-appends replayed actions with `actionActor`, `gameSessionId = sessionReceiptId = activeTrace.gameId`, `startSavedGame(...)` + replayed actions + immediate `writeSavedGame`, `screen = "game"`, clears dialogs, `attachWorkerOrchestrator`, `renderGameScreen()`, `captureOverlayEvent("game.started", …)`, `syncClock()`.
     `resumeSavedGame()` (drops a save this build can't replay), `endGame(reason, completedScore?)` (markAbandoned for non-won/lost, `submitTrace`, `game.ended` analytics, `append_local_score` with `Math.max(0, Math.round(completedScore))`), `finishRun()` (`gameEnded = true`, `dropSavedGame()`, `endGame(won?"won":"lost", score)`, `renderEndCard()`), `endShift(reason = "user_quit")` (endGame, `flushSavedGame()`, leaveGameScreen, clear dialogs, `screen = "menu"`, `cursor = -1`, `drawMenu()`), `restartRun()` (`endGame("restart")`, `dropSavedGame()`, `startRun(selected, variationId)`), `endTone()`, `endCardActionsHtml()` (Play again / export-trace group for arena / Menu), `renderEndCard()` (removes any existing `.game-end-overlay`, appends into `.board`, includes debrief/timeline/evidence/session receipt, focuses `[data-end="restart"]`).
     Also: `let lastRunSeed: number | undefined;`, `handleArenaUi(action: "menu"|"restart"|"help")`, `renderGameScreen` now passes `handleArenaUi` and calls `renderEndCard()` when `gameEnded`, `stepGame` records `if (result.moved && !replaying) recordSavedAction(action)`.
     Input: `handleMenuKey` (`quit`→minimizeToPill, `?`→help), `handleVariationKey` (+`enter`→`chooseVariation`, returns before repainting), `chooseVariation(index)`, `handleGameKey` (game action first, then `quit`→minimize, `r`→restart, `?`→help; delegates to `handleEndCardKey` when over), `handleEndCardKey` (Enter→restart, `q`/`m`→endShift), `handlePauseCardKey` (Enter→minimize, Space/`c`→continue, `m`→endShift, `?`→help), and the restructured `keydown` listener (Escape → `escapeAction`; minimized → return; open dialog → only the paused card takes keys; then gate/menu/variations/scores/settings/game).
     Click delegation added: `data-open-how-to-play`, `data-resume`, `data-restart`, `data-end="restart"|"menu"`, `data-variation-index`, `#inline-back` in game → `endShift`.
     Host listeners + boot: `gamepigeon:launch` → `launchFromHost(detail?.game, detail?.variation)`; `gamepigeon:pause` (gated on `settings.autoPauseOnStop`, uses `pauseForAgent`, focuses `#return-code` unless minimized); `gamepigeon:resume` → `continuePlaying()`; `gamepigeon:reset` (gated on `settings.resetOnNewSession`, endShift if in a game, keeps `minimized`); `launchFromHost` resolves the game/variation and restores from the pill first; `bindWindowChrome(); bindDialogs(); bindUpdateBanner();` + `window.addEventListener("beforeunload", flushSavedGame)`; boot calls `void applyFrame()` then `autoStart()` (`?game=`/`?variation=` deep link else `settings.resumeLastGame && savedGame` → `resumeSavedGame()`), in both the browser and Tauri branches.
   - `/app/overlay/pause-state.test.ts` (created) — 10 tests over the pure transitions (hold semantics, cards stopping the clock, pill holding without un-holding, `escapeAction` routing, immutability).
   - `/app/overlay/tauri-bridge.test.ts` (created) — asserts the four README sizes, expanded > compact, compact ≥ MIN, PILL < MIN (the reason for the setMinSize-first ordering), and that `preview.html` hardcodes `{ width: 600, height: 850 }` and forwards `appParams.set("game"|"variation")`.
   - `/app/overlay/persistence.test.ts` (created) — fake `Storage` (with `failWrites`), a `stubEntry()` PlayableGame double (`left`/`right` move, `wait` never moves, `drop` unknown); covers round-trip, ownerId, blocked writes, garbage/schema rejection, clearing, the 50_000 ceiling, replay filtering, version/id/`create: null` refusals, and `randomSeed` never reusing the previous seed / stepping off a stubbed generator / staying in range.
   - `/app/overlay/session.test.ts` (created) — 22 passing end-to-end tests through one import of app.ts against the real `overlay/dist/index.html`: happy-dom `Window`, stripped `<script>` tags, DOM globals installed, `fetch` stubbed offline, `mock.module("./restaurant-arena-scene.js", …)` capturing `onUi` and counting mounts, `PREVIEW_RESIZE_MESSAGE` listener recording every requested size. Helpers: `settle`, `HOLD_MS = 1_200`, `waitFor`, `press` (dispatched on `document.body`, `bubbles: true`), `host`, `save()`, `landed()` (reads the `gamepigeon:recording:*` journal), `lastResize()`. Groups: starting a run (menu at 600×850, variations, launch + save opened, clock ticks after Space + two `f`), pausing for the agent (host pause holds, Continue playing resumes, host resume), window chrome (pill 144×48 + hold, restore to 600×850, Esc == minimize, resize toggle 830×900 ↔ 600×850 with ↗/↙), cards over the board (help holds the clock, Esc closes it; help opened from the pause card leaves the run held), ending/resuming (menu keeps the save + Resume button; resume replays the same seed and actions; `r` reseeds with empty actions), host launches (named variation, unknown game ignored, reset returns to menu keeping the save), running out the night (debrief with `.game-end-title` matching /Shift (complete|over)/, `[data-session-id]` matching /^game_/, save cleared; Play again; `[data-end="menu"]` → menu with no Resume).

steps.message:
Typecheck is clean and the four overlay test files pass: **53 pass, 0 fail**.

## What was dead, and what it is now

The session lifecycle in `overlay/app.ts` had been amputated below the menu — the render code and the engine were both intact, but nothing connected them. Rebuilt:

**Starting a run** — `startRun(entry, variationId, restored?)` picks a seed via `randomSeed(lastRunSeed)`, creates the game, opens a recording trace (its `gameId` becomes the session receipt id, analytics subject and local-score key), opens the `SavedGame`, mounts the arena and arms the clock. Reachable from the menu → variations flow, `?game=`/`?variation=` deep links, and the host's `gamepigeon:launch`.

**The shift clock** — `syncClock()` arms exactly one scheduler and is called at the end of every `drawGame()`: a deterministic crew gets an app-level `setTimeout` keyed off `game.tickMs()`, a live crew gets `WorkerOrchestrator.start()` (idempotent, so re-entry resumes rather than double-arming). Any hold stops the ticker and calls `orchestrator.pause()`, which clears its timer and aborts in-flight requests.

**Pause/resume** — `gamepigeon:pause` (gated on `settings.autoPauseOnStop`) raises the return prompt and holds the clock; `gamepigeon:resume`, `#continue-game` and Space/`c` hand it back.

**Restart and ending a shift** — `r`, the in-canvas restart and the debrief's Play again all go through `restartRun()`, which ends the old run for the trace, throws the save away and reseeds — `lastRunSeed` guarantees the replacement never re-deals the run it replaced. `gamepigeon:reset`, the in-canvas menu, the pause card's Menu and `#inline-back` go through `endShift()`, which flushes the save and leaves it on disk. Running out the night calls `finishRun()` → debrief overlay with timeline, evidence and a readable `game_…` session id, and the save is dropped since a finished shift isn't resumable.

**Window chrome** — `#hide` collapses to the 144×48 pill (holding the run), the pill restores to whichever frame it came from and re-centers, `#resize` toggles 600×850 ↔ 830×900 with the ↗/↙ glyph and aria-label, and `applySize` sets the minimum *before* the size because the pill is smaller than the 500×700 restored floor. Esc minimizes when no card is up, closes the top card when one is.

**Dialogs** — How to Play and the sign-out confirmation are bound, each card focuses its own `.primary` so Enter does what the button label claims.

**Persistence** — the save is written immediately at launch, appended for accepted non-replay actions on a 2s timer, flushed on `endShift` and `beforeunload`, and dropped on restart/finish/overflow. Sign-out detaches the run in memory but leaves it on disk for the owning account. Boot resumes it when `settings.resumeLastGame` is set, and refuses a save this build can't faithfully replay.

## Tests added

- `overlay/session.test.ts` — 22 tests driving one import of app.ts against the real `overlay/dist/index.html` under happy-dom, with the Phaser scene mocked. Covers launching, the clock actually ticking, holds behind every card, pill/frame sizes, the debrief, resume replaying the same seed, and restart reseeding.
- `overlay/persistence.test.ts`, `overlay/pause-state.test.ts`, `overlay/tauri-bridge.test.ts` — 31 tests over the save record, the pure hold-state machine, and the README size table.

`overlay/session.test.ts` is wired into `test:overlay`.

## Flagging

- **Out of scope, still dead:** the host dispatches `gamepigeon:auth-success`, `gamepigeon:auth-error`, `gamepigeon:sync-error` and `gamepigeon:sync-success` (`tauri/src/main.rs:2217`–`2333`), and the overlay listens for none of them. Sign-*in* completion and sync status therefore never reach the UI.
- **Live-crew resume is inherently partial:** `SavedGame` stores action ids only, so a resumed run replays the player's own actions but not model decisions or interventions. Faithful for a deterministic crew; approximate for a live one. That's the existing schema, not something this change introduced.
- **Dead state:** `lastReplay` in `overlay/app.ts` is declared and never assigned — a leftover from the same amputation, with no replay UI in the shell. Left alone.
- **Pre-existing failures, unrelated:** AppleDouble `._*.test.ts` parse errors (9), `overlay/recording.test.ts > only ever extends the sealed prefix…` (exceeds bun's 5s default), `plugin update checker > keeps the Claude marketplace install on its own updater`, two `npm pack layout` tests, and timing-sensitive `worker-orchestrator.test.ts`. Repo-wide: 547 pass.
